title: A Federated Learning-Based Approach for Improving Intrusion Detection in Industrial Internet of Things Networks
researchArea: Industrial IoT (IIoT) Security, Federated Learning (FL), Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS), Deep Learning (CNN & RNN/LSTM)
problem: Rapid growth in connected IIoT devices generates massive volumes of user data, making conventional centralized machine learning (ML) models impractical due to privacy concerns, excessive wireless bandwidth consumption, latency, and Single Point of Failure (SPOF) risks. Furthermore, resource-constrained IIoT edge devices lack the memory and computational capacity to run heavy security software locally.
motivation: Protecting sensitive IIoT networks (e.g., smart manufacturing, healthcare, smart cities) without centralizing raw network traffic to cloud servers. Deploying FL allows edge devices (such as local Wi-Fi routers) to retain private data locally while sharing only updated model weight parameters with a central aggregator, saving wireless bandwidth and reducing transmission delay.
noveltyAndContributions: Developed an FL-based IIoT Intrusion Detection System combining local deep learning classifiers (CNN and RNN) with central parameter aggregation via FedAvg
Conducted thorough evaluations on the Edge-IIoTset benchmark dataset across 14 attack classes and benign traffic
Evaluated scalability and client performance under both IID and non-IID data distributions with varying client counts (K = 3, 9, 15)
Achieved FL intrusion detection accuracy (92.49%) close to conventional centralized ML models (93.92%) while maintaining data privacy
methodology: Base Classifiers: Convolutional Neural Network (CNN with 2–3 Conv1D layers) and Recurrent Neural Network (RNN/LSTM with 2 hidden LSTM layers)

Data Preprocessing: Removal of missing values and duplicates, flow feature filtering, Z-score normalization, categorical dummy encoding, Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE) for feature selection, and SMOTE for class balancing
FL Aggregation & Training Protocol: Centralized FL architecture executing FedAvg over 50 global communication rounds with 20 local epochs per client
keyAssumptions: The central FL aggregation server is trustworthy
IIoT devices are not malicious or compromised prior to deployment ("No Malicious IIoT Device by Design")
Participating clients (e.g., local gateways/routers) are secure and operate reliably during model training
datasets: Edge-IIoTset: 14 real-world cyberattack types plus normal benign traffic
Attack types: DDoS_UDP, DDoS_ICMP, DDoS_HTTP, DDoS_TCP, Ransomware, SQL_injection, Uploading, Backdoor, Vulnerability_scanner, Port_Scanning, XSS, Password, MITM, Fingerprinting
partition: IID: Dataset classes are evenly and identically distributed across all participant clients
Non-IID: Data distribution across clients is inconsistent and skewed (e.g., some clients hold only a small subset of attack classes)
experimentalSetup: Software: Google Colaboratory, Python 3, NumPy, Pandas, TensorFlow, Keras, Scikit-learn
Hyperparameters: Batch size = 100, Local epochs = 20, Global rounds = 50, Learning rate = 0.01–0.5, Regularization = L2, Loss = categorical_crossentropy, Activation = ReLU, Output = SoftMax
baselines: Centralized ML models: Centralized CNN and Centralized RNN trained on the aggregated dataset
State-of-the-art FL-IDS models from prior literature (Nguyen et al. 2019, Zhao et al. 2020, Li et al. 2021, Huong et al. 2021)
xaiEvaluation: N/A (no explainability method implemented or evaluated)
metrics: False Positive Rate (FPR / False Alarm Rate)
results: Centralized baseline accuracy was 93.92% (Normal class), about 94% overall for both CNN and RNN. FL accuracy at the 50th round, IID: RNN 92.37% / 92.28% / 92.02% and CNN 91.27% / 91.13% / 90.56% for K=3/9/15. Non-IID: RNN 91.87% / 91.53% / 91.07% and CNN 90.58% / 90.73% / 90.18% for K=3/9/15. CNN trains significantly faster than RNN across all client configurations.
failureConditions: Under non-IID data, accuracy disparities between the best and worst clients are severe in early rounds (worst client at round 1 drops to 16.74%–24.64%) due to label skew
Performance degrades if participating clients disconnect mid-operation or have slow upload links
costEvaluation: Theoretical total time complexity is defined as O(total) = O(K·(E·n_k·Σ l_{x-1}·l_x)) + O(K·W) + O(W). Execution time was evaluated empirically across K = 3, 9, 15 for both CNN and RNN. Exact network transmission bytes per round were not reported.

limitations.text: Assumes client devices and aggregation servers are honest; no mechanism to prevent model poisoning attacks from malicious edge nodes. (Authors)
Does not account for resource constraints (battery level, CPU cycle limits, processing speed) when selecting participating clients. (Authors)
Global model accuracy can be negatively impacted by client dropouts during training rounds. (Authors)
The dataset was manually split into synthetic subsets for FL clients because native FL splits for Edge-IIoTset were unavailable.
No Explainable AI framework to interpret feature contributions for detected threat types.
Does not report exact network transmission bytes per round across gRPC channels.

futureWork: Develop outlier detection filtering mechanisms to defend against gradual model poisoning attacks
Design resource-aware FL client selection protocols considering battery backup power, memory, and processing capacity
Mitigate the impact of client dropouts and slow model update transmissions on global model convergence
relevance: Highly relevant benchmark for Edge-FL intrusion detection in IIoT networks, giving comparative baseline metrics on the Edge-IIoTset dataset under IID vs. non-IID distributions using CNN/RNN architectures.
newIdeas: Poisoning-resilient Edge-FL: combine Byzantine-robust aggregation (Krum, Trimmed Mean) with outlier filtering to defend the Edge-IIoTset FL framework against compromised IIoT nodes
XAI-enhanced IIoT intrusion detection: integrate SHAP or LIME with local CNN/RNN models to give analysts interpretable feature attributions for detected attack vectors
Resource-aware dynamic client selection: an energy- and compute-aware selection algorithm to prevent stragglers and client dropouts during FL rounds
